approach_variants.name: The Kindy Creek roadbed and the ribbon-marked climbers' trail to the Point 5116 saddle
approach_variants.notes:
From Marblemount, drive the river road about fourteen miles to the signed forest road 1570 junction and turn right. Cross the river on a concrete bridge and continue about half a mile to a Y-junction where the right fork is blocked by boulders; park there, at roughly 1,150 to 1,300 ft, because a long-standing washout keeps most parties from driving higher.

A climbers' trail flagged with pink ribbon every fifty to a hundred and fifty feet leaves the old roadbed and climbs steeply and directly through old growth - about seventeen hundred vertical feet in its first mile, with few switchbacks - to a ridge saddle near Point 5116. From the saddle the route climbs roughly a thousand feet to Peak 5791, then traverses heather benches and meadows above the lake, crossing or contouring Peak 5860, to reach the base of the east ridge.
hazards: a rooty, eroded and very slick steep mile that is worse descending than ascending
an easy-to-miss junction at the saddle where the two routes on this peak diverge
no water on the steep climb from the roadbed
rolling ridge travel that takes longer than the distance suggests
an exposed camp and no bail-out once out on the ridge
approach_variants.baseFinding:
The junction at the saddle is the whole point of this approach and it is easy to miss. At the ridge saddle near Point 5116, go left and climb about a thousand feet to Peak 5791. If you find yourself dropping toward a lake, or contouring the west side of the crest on a faint tread, you have taken the other branch and are on the Kindy Ridge line that serves the standard route.

The pink ribbon is the handrail on the steep mile below. It is spaced closely enough that losing sight of it for long means you have drifted; the tread is rooty and eroded and very slick when wet, so on the descent the ribbon matters more than the ground does.

Above the saddle the markers are two named high points in order: Peak 5791 first, then heather benches and meadows above the lake, then Peak 5860 crossed or contoured. You should pass two distinct points before the ridge begins - arriving at what you take for the base without having crossed them means you are short.

The base itself is where the east ridge rises out of the ground above the lake basin and runs west toward the summit. If the ground ahead of you is a glacier rather than a ridge, you have contoured past the ridge's foot and joined the standard route's approach to the ice. The east ridge is rock and heather with air on both sides; the standard route crosses snow.

Note that the two routes on this peak describe the ridge junctions differently and one says go left where the other says stay right at a fork. They are not the same fork. Follow the description belonging to the route you intend to climb and use the physical markers - a ribbon-marked steep mile, a saddle, then two high points - rather than reconciling the two.

approach_variants.name: Camping at the lake below the ridge
approach_variants.notes: The lake below the ridge is the common overnight for this route and turns it from a very long day into a comfortable two. The camping is in the meadows on the lake's east side and there is reliable water. Parties doing it in a day still pass through the same ground and should treat the lake as the last water before the ridge.
hazards: loose blocks where the ridge rises out of the benches
committing ridge travel with no easy descent off either side
approach_variants.baseFinding:
From the lake the base of the east ridge is gained by crossing or contouring Peak 5860 and continuing on heather benches above the basin. The ridge foot is where that benched ground runs out against the crest and the rock begins rising west toward the summit.

The test is that you are on a crest, not on a bench. Once established the ground should fall away on both sides. Heather benches with a wall above you and the basin below are still the approach.

And the negative marker is snow. If you are stepping onto glacier ice, you have contoured round past the foot of the ridge and are on the standard route's ground. Turn back and gain the crest.

Carry water from the lake. There is none on the ridge.

waypoints.name: Kindy Creek Trailhead
waypoints.note: Via Kindy Creek Road (FR-1570) off Cascade River Road.
waypoints.directions: From Marblemount, drive the Cascade River Road about 14.2 miles to the signed FR-1570 (Kindy Creek Road) junction and turn right. Cross the Cascade River on a concrete bridge and continue about 0.4 mile to a Y junction where the right fork is blocked by boulders. Park there, at roughly 1,150 to 1,300 feet - a long-standing washout on FR-1570 keeps most parties from driving any higher, so the route starts on foot up the closed roadbed.

waypoints.name: Cyclone Lake
waypoints.note: Common overnight bivy for the East Ridge route.
waypoints.directions: Walk the closed roadbed to where a pink-flagged climbers' trail leaves it and climbs steeply through old growth, about 1,700 ft in the first mile, to a ridge saddle near Point 5116. At this easy-to-miss junction take the branch that climbs about 1,000 ft along Kindy Ridge to Point 5791, then follow the crest over minor humps and heather benches to Cyclone Lake, where the camping is in the meadows on its east side.

waypoints.name: Snowking Mountain - Summit
waypoints.directions: From the lake, cross heather benches and easy slabs onto Snowking's east ridge and follow it west, sidehilling around minor gendarmes and cliff bands and staying off the Snowking Glacier. The final few hundred feet steepen to about 30 degrees on easy snow or scree below the summit block, which is a short Class 3 scramble topping out from the south-southeast.
